Refinement of `beta_share_parity_range_concepts`: people do the same Bayesian concept learning over rules (family-organised prior, exception rules as their own kind), magnitude ranges and odd/even-within-a-range concepts judged as a typical share of the 1–100 line, with the size principle. The one change is that, within the "multiples of m" kind, the rules are no longer equally plausible a priori: people's prior belief in a multiples rule grows (or shrinks) as a power of its base m, with that exponent inferred, so a rule picking out a more specific, larger-base set (multiples of 9, of 12) is favoured over the coarser rule nested in it (multiples of 3, of 4). As a result, after examples such as 36, 45, 54, 81 people say "yes" to other multiples of 9 much more readily than to multiples of 3 that are not multiples of 9 — a stronger preference for the most specific multiplicative rule than the size principle alone gives.

- Inferred per-example stray rate (alpha ~ Beta(9,1), likelihood grouped by (interval size, examples inside)): alpha = 0.890 ± 0.007, LOO -2278.6, p_yes RMSE vs incumbent 0.0085. Submitted as inferred_stray_rate_concepts; it may fail novelty. About 6x slower (147 s vs 25 s).
- One-sided ranges (1..b, a..100) as a third kind: weight 0.003, -2279.1, RMSE 0.005.
- "At most one stray per set" noise: -2586 (much worse). Independent per-example noise is essential, because the model predicts as little as 0.35 "yes" to shown examples (e.g. 83 after 83,38,58,68), and people agree.
**Why:** saves re-testing noise and range-kind variants.
**How to apply:** the fixed ALPHA 0.9 is already optimal. See [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]] and [[concept-space-additions-map]].

name: experiment2-null-refinements
description: experiment2 iter_0 quick-NUTS (2x300) tests — lapse, recall, evidence exponent, parity kind all collapse to the base; calibration near perfect
metadata:
  type: project
---
experiment2 iter_0 (2026-10-30), candidate_5. Quick 2x300 NUTS lppd on the 4500 rows: incumbent gamma_width_exception_family_concepts -2269.2, gamma_width_parity_range_concepts -2270.0.
- Lapse+guess grafted on gamma_width_parity: lapse→0.011, -2270.6.
- example_recall_limited_concepts: recall 0.987, -2286.
- Evidence exponent on the likelihood (LogNormal(0,0.5)): β≈0.97, -2269.2 → would be a near-duplicate.
- Parity-within-range kind weight ≈0.004 on exp2 (unused); calibration by p-bin, set size and participant is near perfect; worst sets look like binomial noise (n=5 cells).
- Submitted doubling_chain_concepts + gamma width (gamma_width_doubling_chain_concepts): -2269.3, chain weight 0.004, novelty RMSE vs gamma_width_parity ≈0.0036 (barely above the 0.002 gate).
- Siblings 3 and 4 both submitted an inferred noise ALPHA this round.
Speed trick: a concept's likelihood depends only on (member count m, examples inside k), so tables count[set,k,group] and per-cell member counts make an evidence exponent cost 8 ms/grad in linear space (exp(β k (gain_m − max_gain)) per (k, group)).
**Why:** exp2 data cannot tell these refinements apart; gains must come from new stimuli.
**How to apply:** don't retry these on exp2; see [[experiment2-data-structure]], [[round4-null-refinements]].

What DID help (submitted as beta_share_width_exception_concepts, iter_0/candidate_3): replacing the gamma width prior with a beta prior over the share (L-0.5)/100, mean ≈0.48 and concentration ≈5.4. Quick LOO -2273.1 vs -2278.4 (+5.2); paired difference +4.6 ± 2.2 grouped by stimulus pair. Largest gain on 43,4,91,9, where near-full ranges are penalised. p_yes RMSE vs incumbent 0.017. Lognormal width: -2281.6 (worse).

description: Adding new rule families to arbitrary_exception_rule_prior barely moves MAP ll (~-1067); which additions were tried
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), adding one new rule family (own Dirichlet weight) to the incumbent arbitrary_exception_rule_prior (MAP ll -1067.0):
- offset residue classes r mod k, k=3..6: -1066.7 (best; submitted as offset_progression_concepts, iter_3/candidate_0)
- same with k up to 12 or 25: -1067.2, weight -> 0
- multiples of 13..50: -1067.8; digit-sum = s: -1067.2 (weight 0.08); odd multiples/2-adic: -1067.2; decade blocks: -1067.3
After 69,9,39,21 the model still predicts 0.61 "yes" for 19 (observed 0/5), even with offset progressions in the space.
**Why:** the concept space is not the bottleneck. Remaining residuals are scattered single cells with n=5.
**How to apply:** don't spend another round on concept-space additions. See [[powers-of-2-37-misfit]].

Round 4 (2026-10-30), iter_4/candidate_1: a rule-vs-range prior log-odds that grows linearly with the number of examples (rule_noticing_grows_with_examples), added to parity_within_range_concepts. def run_candidate_check(
    candidate_dir: Path, responses_path: Path, method: Optional[str] = None
) -> str:
    """Run the admission gates on ``candidate_dir/candidate.py``; return the OK report.

    Raises ``CandidateCheckFailed`` with the same wording admission would use
    (see ``model_zoo._admit_candidate_with_reason``) at the first gate the
    candidate fails.
    """
    candidate_dir = Path(candidate_dir)
    responses_path = Path(responses_path)
    candidate_file = candidate_dir / f"{CANDIDATE_MODULE}.py"
    if not candidate_file.exists():
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"no candidate.py at {candidate_file}")
    if not responses_path.exists():
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"responses CSV not found: {responses_path}")

    forbidden = check_forbidden_imports(candidate_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if forbidden:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"forbidden import: {', '.join(forbidden)} — candidates may only "
            f"import from {sorted(CANDIDATE_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST)}"
        )

    try:
        load_pymc_model(CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"candidate.py is not a loadable PyMC model: {e}"
        ) from e

    fittable, reason = model_logp_is_finite(
        CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir, responses_path
    )
    if not fittable:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"model cannot be fit — {reason}")

    violation = model_contract_violation(
        CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir, responses_path
    )
    if violation is not None:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"model breaks the data contract — {violation}")

    try:
        fit_model(
            CANDIDATE_MODULE,
            candidate_dir,
            responses_path,
            cache_dir=None,
            **CHECK_FIT_KWARGS,
            method=method,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any sampling failure is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"MCMC sampling failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
        ) from e

    # Same sampler settings ⇒ same in-process cache key ⇒ no second fit.
    try:
        loglik = mean_log_likelihood(
            CANDIDATE_MODULE,
            responses_path,
            candidate_dir,
            cache_dir=None,
            **CHECK_FIT_KWARGS,
            method=method,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any failure here is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"log-likelihood computation failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
        ) from e
    if not math.isfinite(loglik):
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"non-finite log-likelihood ({loglik}); a model that assigns ~0 "
            "probability to an observed outcome would corrupt the posterior"
        )

    return (
        f"OK: {candidate_file} loads as a module-level pm.Model, has a finite "
        f"log-probability on {responses_path}, honours the data contract "
        f"(observed = chose_left, p_left = the likelihood's probability), completed a "
        f"{CANDIDATE_CHECK_DRAWS}-draw / {CANDIDATE_CHECK_TUNE}-tune smoke fit "
        f"({CANDIDATE_CHECK_CHAINS} chain) and has a finite log-likelihood ({loglik:.1f} "
        f"on this smoke fit). Not checked here: novelty against the other models."
    )

def run_candidate_check(
    candidate_dir: Path, responses_path: Path, method: Optional[str] = None
) -> str:
    """Run the admission gates on ``candidate_dir/candidate.py``; return the OK report.

    Raises ``CandidateCheckFailed`` with the same wording admission would use
    (see ``model_zoo._admit_candidate_with_reason``) at the first gate the
    candidate fails.
    """
    candidate_dir = Path(candidate_dir)
    responses_path = Path(responses_path)
    candidate_file = candidate_dir / f"{CANDIDATE_MODULE}.py"
    if not candidate_file.exists():
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"no candidate.py at {candidate_file}")
    if not responses_path.exists():
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"responses CSV not found: {responses_path}")

    forbidden = check_forbidden_imports(candidate_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if forbidden:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"forbidden import: {', '.join(forbidden)} — candidates may only "
            f"import from {sorted(CANDIDATE_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST)}"
        )

    try:
        load_pymc_model(CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"candidate.py is not a loadable PyMC model: {e}"
        ) from e

    fittable, reason = model_logp_is_finite(
        CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir, responses_path
    )
    if not fittable:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"model cannot be fit — {reason}")

    violation = model_contract_violation(
        CANDIDATE_MODULE, candidate_dir, responses_path
    )
    if violation is not None:
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(f"model breaks the data contract — {violation}")

    try:
        fit_model(
            CANDIDATE_MODULE,
            candidate_dir,
            responses_path,
            cache_dir=None,
            **CHECK_FIT_KWARGS,
            method=method,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any sampling failure is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"MCMC sampling failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
        ) from e

    # Same sampler settings ⇒ same in-process cache key ⇒ no second fit.
    try:
        loglik = mean_log_likelihood(
            CANDIDATE_MODULE,
            responses_path,
            candidate_dir,
            cache_dir=None,
            **CHECK_FIT_KWARGS,
            method=method,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — any failure here is the reason
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"log-likelihood computation failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
        ) from e
    if not math.isfinite(loglik):
        raise CandidateCheckFailed(
            f"non-finite log-likelihood ({loglik}); a model that assigns ~0 "
            "probability to an observed outcome would corrupt the posterior"
        )

    return (
        f"OK: {candidate_file} loads as a module-level pm.Model, has a finite "
        f"log-probability on {responses_path}, honours the data contract "
        f"(observed = chose_left, p_left = the likelihood's probability), completed a "
        f"{CANDIDATE_CHECK_DRAWS}-draw / {CANDIDATE_CHECK_TUNE}-tune smoke fit "
        f"({CANDIDATE_CHECK_CHAINS} chain) and has a finite log-likelihood ({loglik:.1f} "
        f"on this smoke fit). Not checked here: novelty against the other models."
    )

I've written the repair candidate, `beta_share_without_replacement_concepts`, and it passes the admission check. It should clear the novelty gate too, though it fits a little worse than the incumbent.

**What it is:** a refinement of `without_replacement_sampling_concepts`. People assume the program never repeats a number, so each new example is one of the concept's members not yet shown. The one change is the range-width prior: it now uses the incumbent's beta prior over the share of the 1–100 line a range covers, in place of the gamma prior over raw width. This speaks to the critique's nested-multiples gap. When the examples use up a good part of a small rule (36, 45, 54, 81 out of the multiples of 9), the model favours that rule over the broader one around it (multiples of 3) more strongly than sampling with replacement does.

**Why I dropped my first idea:** I first tried adding the inferred stray rate (how often an example is a random number) to the beta-share model. It inferred a rate of 0.898, almost exactly the incumbent's fixed 0.9. Its predictions then sat only 0.0021 RMSE from the incumbent, right at the 0.002 limit, and this is the last attempt for the slot. The new model's change is built in, with no parameter that can shrink back to the incumbent.

- **Novelty:** I fitted the five closest live models (one chain, 300 draws each) and compared average predictions on the observed trials. This is not the gate's own 512-stimulus pool. The new model is 0.0106–0.0154 RMSE from all five, the closest being `uncertainty_shifted_criterion` (0.0106) and the incumbent (0.0118). The original `without_replacement_sampling_concepts` wasn't in that comparison, but it uses the old gamma width prior, and switching that prior moved predictions by 0.017 last time.
- **Fit:** in-sample log-likelihood is −2267.1 against the incumbent's −2264.3, about 2.8 nats worse. So it probably won't overtake the incumbent; it tests whether the sampling assumption holds up once the width prior is better.
- **Admission check:** OK, smoke-fit log-likelihood −2271.6, sampling took 11 s. Convergence (R-hat, ESS) was not checked; that only happens in the full fit.
